extracted.intended_audience: federal agency officials responsible for rulemaking, tribal consultation, and OMB reviewers
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural requirements (under Executive Order 13175) that federal agencies must follow when developing policies, regulations, or actions that have tribal implications, including consultation process design, documentation, cost/preemption considerations, and OMB certification. Targets agency staff who draft rules, designate consultation officials, and submit rules to OMB.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect for Indian tribal self-government and sovereignty
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must respect Indian tribal self-government and sovereignty in policymaking that has tribal implications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embedded principle: policy development should acknowledge tribal authority and sovereignty as a baseline consideration when rules affect tribes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultation on need for Federal standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must consult with tribal officials on the need for Federal standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consultation should occur to assess whether Federal standards are necessary before imposing them; part of meaningful engagement with tribal officials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide maximum administrative discretion where tribes administer Federal programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should provide 'the maximum administrative discretion possible' where Indian tribal governments administer Federal statutes and regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preference for flexible implementation approaches that allow tribal governments discretion in administering federal programs affecting them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage: definition of 'policies with tribal implications'
rubrics_metrics.description: The EO covers 'regulations, legislative comments or proposed legislation, and other policy statements or actions that have substantial direct effects on one or more Indian tribes, on the relationship between the Federal government and Indian tribes, or on the distribution of power and responsibilities between the Federal Government and Indian tribes.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this definition to determine whether a proposed action triggers the EO's consultation and documentation requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accountable consultation process requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must have an 'accountable process to ensure meaningful and timely input by tribal officials in the development of regulatory policies that have tribal implications.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Process must be both meaningful (substantive, not perfunctory) and timely (early enough to influence policy development); agencies should be able to demonstrate accountability in how input was solicited and considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of Tribal Consultation and Coordination Official
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must designate an official principally responsible for implementing the EO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This official certifies compliance to OMB and is the accountable point of contact for tribal consultation activities; agencies should document the designation and responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on issuing rules that impose substantial direct compliance costs
rubrics_metrics.description: To the extent practicable and permitted by law, agencies shall not issue rules with tribal implications that impose 'substantial direct compliance costs on Indian tribal governments,' if not required by statute, unless they either (a) provide funds for those costs or (b) comply with tribal summary impact statement requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before issuing costly rules, agencies should either secure federal funding to cover direct compliance costs or prepare and disclose a tribal summary impact statement and evidence of consultation; avoid imposing unfunded mandates on tribes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on preempting tribal law
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies shall not issue rules with tribal implications that preempt tribal law, unless they comply with the tribal summary impact statement requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a rule would preempt tribal law, agencies must follow the stronger documentation/consultation steps (tribal summary impact statement) to justify the preemption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of funds for direct compliance costs
rubrics_metrics.description: If an agency issues a rule that imposes direct compliance costs on Indian tribal governments, the Federal government must provide money for those direct compliance costs (where practicable and permitted by law).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should seek or identify funding sources to cover tribal compliance costs when feasible; absence of funds triggers alternative compliance steps (e.g., impact statement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Tribal Summary Impact Statement — early consultation
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must consult with tribal officials 'early in the process of developing the proposed regulation' as part of the tribal summary impact statement requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early engagement is required (not after key decisions); document timing and substance of early consultations in the summary impact statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tribal Summary Impact Statement — preamble content
rubrics_metrics.description: In a separately identified portion of the rule’s preamble, agencies must provide a tribal summary impact statement describing (a) the prior consultations with tribal officials, (b) the nature of the officials’ concerns and the agencies’ justification for the rule, and (c) the extent to which the concerns have been met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preamble must explicitly include these three elements in a distinct section so readers and OMB can assess the consultation record and agencies' responses to tribal concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tribal Summary Impact Statement — written communications availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must make available to OMB tribal officials’ written communications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain and provide to OMB the written record of tribal communications (letters, emails, comments) as part of the consultation documentation required under the EO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of consensual mechanisms for certain issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must use consensual mechanisms, including negotiated rulemaking, where appropriate, for developing regulations on issues relating to tribal self-government, tribal trust resources, or Indian tribal treaty and other rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the subject matter implicates tribal governance, trust resources, or treaty rights, agencies should favor collaborative, consensus-based rulemaking processes rather than adversarial approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Streamline waivers and consider flexible policy approaches
rubrics_metrics.description: As appropriate, practicable, and permitted by law, agencies must streamline the processes for waivers of statutes and rules for Indian tribes, consider increasing opportunities for using 'flexible policy approaches,' and make decisions on waivers within 120 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should adopt expedited waiver procedures and be prepared to offer flexible alternatives to standard rule application for tribes; track timing to meet the 120-day decision expectation.

rubrics_metrics.name: OMB certification requirement for rules with tribal implications
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies submitting to OMB under EO 12866 final rules with tribal implications must include a certification from their Tribal Consultation and Coordination Official that this EO’s requirements were 'met in a meaningful and timely manner.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before sending final rules to OMB, obtain and include the consultation official's written certification confirming compliance with EO 13175; this is part of OMB review documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability encouragement to independent regulatory agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Independent regulatory agencies are encouraged to comply with the provisions of this order (see § 8).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While not mandatory for independent agencies, the EO explicitly encourages them to follow these consultation principles and procedures; documentation of voluntary compliance may be appropriate.
